## What changes when we move the centre? {#fv6-centre .fv-lesson .circle-lesson }

```{=html}
<div class="circle-top-form"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{r}(\theta)=\underset{\sim}{c}+R\cos\theta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+R\sin\theta\,\underset{\sim}{j}"></span></div><div data-circle-visual="centre"></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §3.5 · p. 69</div>

::: {.notes}
Use Next construction to show OC=c (teal), then CP (gold), then OP=r (blue). The point is amber; coordinate captions sit below the graph. C=(2,−1), R=3. Ask: which part is fixed, and which part changes with θ? The radius vector rotates with constant length R. Adding it to c gives a vector pointing to every point of the translated circle. At a complete construction, move the angle slider and follow the endpoint. Previous reverses each reveal; Reset returns to θ=π/3 and no vectors.
:::
